Carriers are defined by their ability to launch and manage smaller spacecraft.

Navigating complex environments emphasizes creativity and teamwork.
Escorts rely on speed and agility to fulfill their defensive roles.
Purpose: Balances scouting and defensive support, ideal for locating threats and protecting the fleet.

◦ Light Plasma Cannons: For small-scale threats. ▪ Range: 3,000 km. ▪ Damage: 3d6 per shot. ▪ Cooldown: None; can fire every turn. ◦ Countermeasure Launcher: Disrupt incoming projectiles or lock-ons. ▪ Effect: Enemy attacks within 1,000 km roll at disadvantage for 1 turn. ▪ Cooldown: 2 turns.
While not primarily combat-oriented, Explorer ships have basic defenses for self-protection.
◦ Can self-destruct for massive damage. ▪ Range: Adjacent to the target. ▪ Damage: 6d8 in a 500-meter radius. ▪ Special: Target must make a Dexterity save (DC 15) to halve damage.

◦ Focus attacks on bombers or missile carriers. ▪ Subsystem Targeting: Spend an action to target enemy payloads. •Roll: D20 + Gunnery modifier. •DC: Based on enemy size and distance (e.g., 15 for bombers, 18 for larger ships). •Success: Neutralize bombs, missiles, or torpedoes.
Interceptors specialize in countering smaller, faster threats like fighters and bombers.

Logistics ships are designed to be highly customizable for specific missions.

•Quick Patch: Provide 10 HP repair to an allied ship (temporary). •Stabilize Systems: Prevent subsystem failure with an Engineering roll (DC 15-20). •Deploy Repair Drones: Send automated drones to repair an ally at a distance.

🧠 Digital Defense & Electronic Warfare (EW) Hangars with advanced systems are vulnerable to hacking, jamming, and sabotage. The following systems help maintain digital security: Tactical Controller 15,000 5 credits/day Grants reroll on 1 defense check per encounter

When EP needs exceed supply: •Brownout: Systems draw only 50% efficiency (e.g., only half repairs/mods succeed). •Blackout: If EP falls below 20% of demand, systems shut down. Must reboot (takes 1 Base Turn). •Overdrawn Capacitor: If output exceeds the discharge rate, roll a Stability Check (DC 15): ◦ On fail: capacitor shorts and cannot be used for 1 Base Turn. ◦ On success: system stabilizes, but charge rate is halved next turn.

Each Base Turn, players may designate power routing: •Priority to Repair: +5 bonus HP repaired to all repair tasks. •Priority to Modding: +1 to modding checks, and up to two mods can be processed simultaneously. •Priority to Construction: Halve material requirements or time needed for manufacturing. •Balanced Mode: All functions run as normal. •Power Saving Mode: Reduces all power usage by 25%, but delays all actions by 1 turn. Changing power modes requires a technicianʼs full shift or a control override check (DC 12 Engineering).

Mechas can be modified in the field under emergency conditions using the Rapid Mod Protocol: •Takes 1 action per mod slot (max 2 per turn) •Requires a successful Engineering or Craft check (DC 18) •Failure = install works, but inflicts 1d4 strain to the mecha This may be useful during long missions where access to hangars is limited, or if the partyʼs mobile base has a Mini-Modding Bay.
overload—1d4 systems lose power for 1 turn or must reroute.

Each Base Turn, hangars perform Readiness Checks for all mechas in storage. This determines how quickly they can launch and whether latent damage or errors have developed. Readiness Roll (d20): •DC 10 for stored mechas in Active Mode with a mechanic assigned
Stored mechas can be kept in Standby Mode (low maintenance) or Active Mode (combat-ready). Switching modes takes 1 hour, or 2 rounds during combat with a successful Engineering check (DC 15).
